answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post, 'NVIDIA Unlocks AI Compute at Scale, Inviting Partners to Power the AI Infrastructure Buildout', published 2026-07-01 (party statement, company publisher). Includes a quoted statement from Sharon AI's CEO James Manning and a Firmus project description, both relayed through NVIDIA's blog.
answer.note: NVIDIA states it is introducing a business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers, supported by a revenue-sharing and credit-support structure. Under this model, NVIDIA would earn standard product revenue plus a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity, which NVIDIA describes as a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream. This is evidence of NVIDIA's stated strategy and intended revenue channels for NVDA. It does not establish the size of any revenue share, credit-support exposure, contract volumes or timing. The Firmus Batam campus (expected 360 MW and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs) and the Sharon AI and AI-cloud DSX factory statements are developer or partner plans, and they indicate demand-side and supply-side activity that is consistent with the model, not confirmed NVIDIA orders or revenue. Overall, the source supports a conditional read that NVIDIA is shifting part of its go-to-market toward partner-financed AI cloud capacity with revenue participation, with the financial effect unquantified.
limitations: The revenue-share percentage, duration, and cloud revenue base on which NVIDIA's share would apply are not disclosed.
The credit-support amounts, counterparties' obligations, and NVIDIA's maximum exposure under the credit-support component are not disclosed.
It is not disclosed whether any specific AI cloud has signed an agreement under this model; the source describes partnering and building but does not state signed contract status.
The 360 MW and 170,000 GPU Firmus figures are described as expected scale, with no disclosed timeline, financing, or completion status.
The source is NVIDIA's own promotional blog, so the characterization of the model's benefits and NVIDIA's earnings channels is company-authored and not independently verified.
No quantified NVIDIA revenue, margin, or backlog effect from this model is given.
follow_up: Check NVIDIA's next annual report (10-K) and quarterly filings for disclosure of revenue-share arrangements, credit guarantees, or customer financing commitments tied to AI cloud partners.
Search for signed or announced agreements between NVIDIA and named AI clouds (Sharon AI, Firmus, and others) to establish whether any contracts beyond the blog post exist.
Check Firmus and Sharon AI public filings or announcements for financing, construction milestones, and GPU delivery schedules for the Batam campus and related projects.
Review NVIDIA's accounting disclosures for guarantees or contingent liabilities that could capture credit-support exposure once any such arrangements are reported.
